judged_text: Lark's createEvent (and identically createAttendees, updateEvent and deleteEvent) resolves the calendar from destinationCalendar[0] instead of the destination matching the executing credential, so the per-credential selection was not carried over. For a COLLECTIVE booking with multiple Lark hosts, every per-host createEvent call targets the first host's calendar, so the other hosts' calendars never receive the event and the first host's calendar can receive duplicates.

record.issue_text: [BUG] Lark's createEvent (and identically createAttendees, updateEvent and deleteEvent) resolves the calendar from destinationCalendar[0] instead of the destination matching the executing credential, so the per-credential selection was not carried over. For a COLLECTIVE booking with multiple Lark hosts, every per-host createEvent call targets the first host's calendar, so the other hosts' calendars never receive the event and the first host's calendar can receive duplicates.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent`, `createAttendees`, `updateEvent`, and `deleteEvent` all derive `calendarId` from `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`, i.e. always the first destination calendar. Meanwhile `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(...)` per destination/credential, intending per-host/per-credential targeting. Because Lark always uses `[0]`, every per-host call will target the first host's calendar, causing missing events for other hosts and potential duplicates on the first host.
